newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee dips on overseas strength of dlr.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee dips on overseas strength of dlr.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee opened down as speculators bought dollars due to overseas gains by the greenback, dealers said.
At 0500 GMT the rupee was at its opening level of 57.84 to the dollar. The rupee closed at 57.77 on Tuesday.
"The rupee which opened low as banks had factored in overseas gains by the dollar, fell to 57.90 when the Central Bank pushed up the dollar," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The local currency regained some ground when banks sold dollars aggressively close to the 57.90 level, he said.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 4.25 local cents, fixing buying and selling rates at 57.0502 and 58.2028.
Overnight call money rates, which were moving in a tight range, were at 12.75 percent after opening at 13 percent, dealers said.
"I can't see money rates rising even if lenders hold back, because there are few borrowers," said a Citibank dealer.
Lenders who hold back will have to eventually sell rupees to the Central Bank at the overnight repurchase rate of 10.50 percent, he said.
